solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Affected by brilliance all the rage in act, invites around

indicators.note: HOT is placed inside POSE
INVITES is turned around into a new order

blocks.note: to pose is to put on an act
something all the rage is hot
INVITES rearranged

explanation.surface: A performance so fashionable that it draws invitations from all sides, and someone is dazzled by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brilliance' suggests genius or a dazzling show; here it is simply bright light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something photosensitive reacts to light, so it is affected by brilliance.

clue.text: Source of sterility in badly-written Utopian satires

indicators.note: the letters are set down in a jumbled order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Poorly composed satires about ideal worlds are what makes a reader lose the will to create.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sterility' suggests barren writing, but here it is the germ-free state of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasteurisation heats milk to kill microbes, making it sterile.

clue.text: Omit tasteless stuff before disturbing recitation of dreams

indicators.note: to omit something is to leave it out, so TAT is dropped from the word that follows
the remaining letters of RECITATION are stirred up

blocks.note: the word itself, before cutting
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut vulgar material before a troubling reading about dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove TAT from RECITATION to leave RECIION, then rearrange those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the Greek oneiros, a dream: oneiric describes anything dreamlike or belonging to dreams.

clue.text: Men embarrassed over request

indicators.note: in a down clue, RED is turned over so it reads upwards

blocks.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
embarrassed people go red

explanation.surface: Some men are left blushing by what they have been asked to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' here are OR, the other ranks of the army, a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you order a meal or goods, which is to ask for them.

clue.text: Viewer’s support certainly needed in European discussion

indicators.note: YES must go inside E TALK

blocks.note: E is the usual abbreviation
'certainly!' means yes
a discussion is a talk

explanation.surface: A viewer's backing is essential if talks in Europe are to go anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' suggests a TV audience; here it is an eye, and the support is the stalk that holds it up.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyestalk is the stalk on which a crab's or snail's eye is carried.

clue.text: Small domestic fowl finish off fruit

indicators.note: the final letter of SULTANA is taken off

blocks.note: a sultana is a dried grape

explanation.surface: A little chicken polishes off some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: SULTAN is also a small ornamental breed of chicken, white and crested, which is the fowl meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The sultan is a small fancy breed of domestic chicken originally from Turkey.

clue.text: What duke has attendant beginning to work?

blocks.note: a duke holds a title
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of servant a duke keeps to begin the day's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a written work, a book, whose opening leaf is the title page.
explanation.definitionFit: The title page is the first page of a book, the start of the work.

clue.text: Meat cooker missing lid is working

indicators.note: in a down clue the top letter is the lid, so OVEN loses its O

blocks.note: OVEN without its first letter
used as it stands
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: The meat is cooking even though the oven has no lid on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid' only works because this is a down clue: the top of the vertical word is its lid.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat by category: venison is the flesh of deer, served as game.

clue.text: Like a line that goes straight? No main line does, sadly

definitions.text: Like a line that goes straight?

indicators.note: the letters end up in a sorry state, out of order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lament about railways: no main line runs straight any more.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: a straight line has length but no width, and 'line' seems to be about railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric line has only length, so it is one-dimensional.

clue.text: Veronica’s in good health following career

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so WELL is placed after SPEED

blocks.note: to career is to rush along; speed
someone in good health is well

explanation.surface: A woman named Veronica is fit and well after starting her working life.
explanation.walkthrough: Veronica looks like a woman's name, but it is the botanical genus of the speedwell plant. 'Career' is the verb, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwells are the flowering plants of the genus Veronica.

clue.text: Join backing group

indicators.note: to back is to move backwards, so NONET is read from its end

blocks.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: An invitation to become part of a band's backing group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing group' reads as a band behind a singer; 'backing' is the instruction and 'Join' is a noun, a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the tongue of a mortise-and-tenon join in woodwork.

clue.text: A little fear or remorse over slip-up

indicators.note: only a small part of the phrase is used
that part is read backwards

blocks.note: feaR OR REmorse, read right to left

explanation.surface: Someone feels a touch of fear and regret after a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The last R of fear, OR, and the RE of remorse read backwards spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a slip-up is a small mistake, and a mistake of any size is an error.

clue.text: Came across piece of poetry set in jazzy style

indicators.note: VERSE is placed inside TRAD

blocks.note: trad is traditional jazz
a verse is a unit of a poem

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled upon a poem written to a jazz rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came across' suggests finding by chance; here it means crossed over.
explanation.definitionFit: The literal sense of 'came across' is wanted: a traveller who crossed a desert traversed it.

clue.text: A drop of chalk, say, in cataract on Hudson?

indicators.note: in an across clue, FALL sits on ROCK by coming after it

blocks.note: Rock Hudson was a Hollywood film star
a cataract is a waterfall, a fall

explanation.surface: A drop of chalk tumbles into a waterfall on the Hudson River.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hudson looks like the New York river; it is the actor Rock Hudson. Chalk is an example of rock, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockfall is a mass of rock, such as chalk, dropping from a cliff.

clue.text: Lucky having strength to catch large fish

indicators.note: FORTE takes TUNA inside it

blocks.note: one's forte is one's strong point
the tuna is a big sea fish

explanation.surface: An angler is lucky to be strong enough to land a big fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strength' is a forte in the sense of a strong point, not physical power.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone favoured by fortune is lucky.

clue.text: Firearm’s a variety of gun carried by French gentlemen

indicators.note: GUN comes in another form, GNU
what is carried is held within the carrier, so MM holds A GNU

blocks.note: MM abbreviates Messieurs, French for gentlemen
used as it stands
GUN rearranged

explanation.surface: A pistol, one of a type of gun carried by gentlemen in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of gun' reads as a kind of weapon; 'a' stays put while GUN is reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a powerful handgun or its cartridge.

clue.text: Half of West End area accepts a new contract

indicators.note: COVENT takes A N inside it

blocks.note: Covent Garden is a West End district of London; the first half of its name
used as it stands
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Part of London's theatre district signs up to a fresh deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre and shopping district; Covent Garden is one area in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym with a legal flavour: a covenant is a binding agreement, often in a deed.

clue.text: Tie up dog during visit

indicators.note: what happens during something falls within its span, so CUR goes inside SEE

blocks.note: to see someone is to visit them
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone tethers their dog while they pay a call.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Tie up dog' one phrase; 'Tie up' is the definition and the dog goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you secure a boat or a parcel by fastening it.

clue.text: Large crater in Central America sheltering tree

indicators.note: CA protects ALDER by holding it inside

blocks.note: CA is the abbreviation
the alder is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree grows in the shelter of a vast crater somewhere in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places the crater in Central America; that phrase is only CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical term: a caldera is the wide crater left when a volcano collapses.

clue.text: Alert because of conflict between bridge opponents

indicators.note: something between two things sits in the gap, so WAR goes inside E N

blocks.note: 'for' can mean because of
at bridge, East and North sit next to each other on opposing sides
war is conflict

explanation.surface: A warning issued because a card game has turned into a quarrel between rival players.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge partners are North-South and East-West, so East and North are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense of 'Alert': to forewarn is to warn in advance.

clue.text: Advanced series of steps in audition for dancer

indicators.note: we hear the words rather than read them

blocks.note: A is advanced; a stair is a flight of steps

explanation.surface: A dancer auditions with a sophisticated sequence of dance steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Series of steps' suggests a dance routine, which fits the audition; here it is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was the celebrated Hollywood dancer.

clue.text: Five in a horse race with no unknown, perhaps unusually

indicators.note: the five is put in, so V goes inside A DERB
the Y is removed from DERBY

blocks.note: used as it stands
the Derby, minus Y
Y is a mathematical unknown, removed
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five horses run in a race without an outsider, perhaps oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps unusually' is the definition by example: 'unusually' is an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Unusually' is one example of an adverb, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Dorset village scheme turned to chaos, losing millions

indicators.note: something turned is flipped round, so PLOT reads backwards
something losing a part lets it go, so MUDDLE drops its M

blocks.note: a plot is a scheme
a muddle is chaos
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A plan in a Dorset village descends into chaos and loses a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorset is a county in southwest England; the village is famous for the Tolpuddle Martyrs, early trade unionists.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Tolpuddle is one of many villages in the county of Dorset.

clue.text: For beginners, take up the trombone in passage all play

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of each word

blocks.note: Take Up The Trombone In

explanation.surface: A tip for novices: take up the trombone in a piece where the whole band plays.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a musical direction: a passage in which all performers play together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti, Italian for 'all', marks a passage played by the whole orchestra.

clue.text: Old noble in northeastern Kent mainly

indicators.note: most of THANET is used, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: the Isle of Thanet is the northeastern tip of Kent

explanation.surface: An aristocrat of long ago lived mostly in the northeast of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in southeast England; Thanet, once an island, is its northeast corner, home to Margate and Ramsgate.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was a nobleman in Anglo-Saxon England or Scotland.

clue.text: Pope dismissing foremost artist’s work for stage

indicators.note: POPE drops its first letter

blocks.note: POPE without the P
an RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A pope sacks his leading painter, whose work is for the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dismissing foremost' seems to mean sacking a top artist; it only removes the first letter of Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: an opera is one kind of dramatic work written to be staged.

clue.text: Radiation possibly is weak round about an atom that’s charged

indicators.note: to turn round is to face backwards, so TAME reads EMAT
about means surrounding, so EMAT is placed about AN

blocks.note: tame means feeble or weak
used as it stands
an ion is an electrically charged atom

explanation.surface: A physics note: radiation is feeble around a charged atom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is weak' looks like part of the physics statement; 'is' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something given off, and radiation is one example.

clue.text: Collected beside Iris Murdoch novel delivered just in time

blocks.note: savings are collected up
by means next to, beside
The Bell is a 1958 novel by Iris Murdoch

explanation.surface: Someone picks up an Iris Murdoch novel that arrived just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests a parcel; it means rescued, as a boxer is saved by the bell ending the round.
explanation.definitionFit: To be saved by the bell is to be rescued at the last moment.
